papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

description.text:
Fine-tuned by SpaceXerror as part of ongoing research on domain-specific LLM adaptation for mental health support.

This model was developed as part of a research paper investigating the effectiveness of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods — specifically QLoRA — for adapting large language models to mental health support tasks.

output_type.quote: You are a compassionate, empathetic mental health support assistant.

use_claim.quote: You are a compassionate, empathetic mental health support assistant. You listen carefully, validate feelings, and provide thoughtful, evidence-based guidance.

warning.quote: This model is NOT a replacement for professional therapy or crisis intervention.

serving.system_prompt:
You are a compassionate, empathetic mental health support assistant.
You listen carefully, validate feelings, and provide thoughtful, evidence-based guidance.
Always prioritize the person's safety and wellbeing.
serving.notes: generation_config.json sets only bos_token_id and eos_token_id. The sampling values above are the card's usage example. config.json max_position_embeddings is 32768. The tokenizer model_max_length is an unset sentinel, not a context length. Training truncated sequences at 512. The Hub library tag is peft and the tags include base_model:adapter, but the repository has three float16 weight shards and no adapter_config.json. The notebook formatted CounselChat with a longer system prompt than the card's example. PHR rows were kept in their original Llama-2 chat text, including a different system string. The notebook file contains a hard-coded Hub token; it is not copied here.

evaluation_reported.text: The card and the notebook log both report train loss 0.8180 and perplexity 2.451 on 200 held-out samples (2.359 at 50, 2.439 at 100, 2.438 at 150). The card also lists a final validation loss of 0.7862. No external benchmark is named. The card says the research paper is in progress.

discrepancies: Inventory methods are full_finetune|qlora. The card and the executed notebook describe QLoRA on a 4-bit NF4 base, then a merge of the adapter into a float16 copy of the base. The card sentence 'QLoRA enables full fine-tuning of 7B models on 2× Tesla T4 GPUs' is about QLoRA, not a full-parameter update. Dataset ids and the parent match. The card's sample counts do not match the notebook log. The card says 2,598 CounselChat and 4,527 PHR, totaling 7,125, with a 6,768/357 split. The notebook kept 2,598 of 2,775 CounselChat rows and 25,838 of 99,086 PHR rows, capped that mix at 15,000 (14,250 train / 750 val), and passed 7,125 train rows and 375 val rows to SFTTrainer. The card's frozen-parameter line, 3.758B and 1.1% trainable, repeats a quantized parameter count from the notebook. The same notebook's PEFT summary says 41,943,040 trainable parameters of 7,289,966,592 (0.5754%). The uploaded safetensors total is 7,248,023,552 float16 parameters.
